c.tagline: Cobblestoned colonial time capsule where pastel mansions meet Caribbean beaches

taxi.color: pink/yellow classic cars & modern private taxis
taxi.fareNote: Meters are essentially nonexistent; agree on a price in cash (USD/EUR preferred) before you get in. Vintage American cars double as shared 'colectivo' taxis on fixed routes.

emergency.note: Police 106, ambulance 104, fire 105. Bring your own basic medical supplies — pharmacies are frequently under-stocked; travel insurance covering medical evacuation is strongly advised.

hood_landmark.Plaza Mayor: Iglesia Parroquial de la Santísima Trinidad
hood_landmark.Barrio La Popa: Ermita de Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria de la Popa
hood_landmark.Calle Colón / San Procopio: Casa de la Música outdoor steps

avoid.reason: Persistent jineteros (street hustlers) push commissions on casas and restaurants, and cobbled streets are poorly lit at night.

hood_desc: The UNESCO-listed historic heart: ochre cobblestones, terracotta roofs, and the mustard-yellow bell tower of the Convento de San Francisco. Museums, colonial mansions, and the main square anchor every visitor's first stop.
A quieter hillside quarter above the center, named for the small Ermita chapel, with sweeping views over Trinidad's rooftops to the Escambray Mountains. Fewer tourists, more everyday Trinidad life.
Home to grand 19th-century sugar-baron mansions like the Palacio Cantero, whose tower offers the best rooftop panorama in town. A mix of museums and family-run casas particulares.
Trinidad's after-dark hub, centered on the open-air stone steps of the Casa de la Música where locals and travelers dance to live son and salsa most nights under the stars.
A powder-white Caribbean beach about 12 km south of town, with turquoise water, beach clubs, and snorkeling — the classic day-trip pairing with Trinidad's colonial streets.

water.note: Stick to bottled or filtered water; supply and treatment are unreliable.

transit.map: No formal transit map; the historic center is small enough to walk end-to-end in 20 minutes
transit.note: There's no real public transit system in the historic center — walking, bici-taxis, and shared 'almendrones' (classic car colectivos) cover local trips, with a small tourist bus linking downtown to Playa Ancón.

air: Alberto Delgado Airport (TND, very limited/seasonal service)
José Martí International Airport, Havana (HAV, main gateway)
train: Historic Valle de los Ingenios tourist steam train (excursion only, not regular transport)
bus: Viazul tourist buses connect Havana, Cienfuegos, and Varadero to Trinidad

tip.r: Tipping is an essential part of Cuba's tourism economy where state wages are very low; 10% at restaurants, small cash tips for casa particular hosts, musicians, and guides are the norm.
